procedure_summary: Esterification of the benzoic acid with cyclohexane-1,3-dione to the enol ester, drawn with no reagent on the arrow.
notes: The middle transformation of the composite step (vi), drawn at lines 141 and 151. In both of those spans the vision read splits it across two entries, step_id 2 carrying the acid as a reactant with an empty products list and step_id 3 carrying the ester as a product with an empty reactants list, which is one arrow read as two halves rather than two transformations; it is annotated here as the single transformation the two halves describe. Cyclohexane-1,3-dione is recorded as a reactant even though neither of those two spans reads a reagent on the arrow: the drawn product is its enol ester, and the same compound is read explicitly on the companion schemes at lines 99 and 153, so leaving it out would make the record chemically impossible rather than merely incomplete. No coupling agent, acid chloride, base, solvent or temperature is stated in this section for the step; the background route reached the same ester through an acid chloride, and this section says nothing about how it is done here. procedure_summary: Rearrangement of the enol ester to the ring-acylated triketone, which is the target herbicide and the last transformation of the route.
notes: The closing transformation of both composite steps (vi) and (vi'), drawn at lines 141, 143, 151 and 153, in every case with a bare arrow and no reagent read. Ester and product share the molecular formula C17H16ClF3O6S as read from the drawings, an isomerisation: the aroyl group migrates from the enol oxygen to the ring carbon to give the 2-aroylcyclohexane-1,3-dione. reaction_class is other because the enum offers no rearrangement term and forcing it into acylation would misdescribe an intramolecular migration as an intermolecular acyl transfer; the tag transformation:rearrangement carries the reading. named_reaction is left null: this is a Fries-type rearrangement by analogy rather than a Fries rearrangement, and the rule says not to stretch for a name. precursor_step names scheme step 7 because that is the step that precedes it in the composite (vi), but scheme step 6 produces the same ester by the shorter branch and is an equally valid precursor; the field holds one value, so the alternative is recorded here. [0020] and [0022] state the step may be run in one pot with the preceding esterification, without isolating the intermediate ester compound; is_one_pot is false on this single-transformation record for the reason given on scheme step 7. tembotrione is the only compound in this section the prose names in words.
